about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

corpus-map.json.note: #102 (the engine's finding 17) corrected game-value's ambiguity question to name both cases where the gammon and backgammon conditions overlap, a man up and a man in the winner's home table with nothing borne off; narrowed its gap case to a man outside both home tables; and added to its note both overlap cases as demonstrations and why 'begun to bear off' means removal. No other entry changed. It is a semantic change, so it carries an independent verdict and not an exemption. The verdict file names these bytes and records three rounds. previousReview is the blind-second-mapping review of the map #95 left (previousSha256), unchanged.

previousReview.note: Issue #95. compare.py read the map at 32c5a69 (32 entries), the bytes the legacy exemption covered, and exits 1 unless each of its 127 flags has a row in resolutions.json. The map was corrected to those rows (18 blind-right, 5 corpus-does-not-settle; 33 entries) in the same commit that replaced the exemption with this review. sha256 is the corrected map; compared.sha256 is the map before correction. The blind mapper worked from docs with every backgammon example removed (blind-mapping/REDACTIONS.md); what could not be ruled out is in blind-mapping/README.md, Limits.
